robert.title: This doll gets apology letters

slides.text: THIS DOLL GETS APOLOGY LETTERS
Key West, Florida. A 40-inch handmade doll in a sailor suit, stuffed with excelsior. His name is Robert.
He belonged to Key West artist Gene Otto. Whenever something went wrong in that house, the excuse was always the same: "Robert did it."
Gene kept Robert his whole life. He died in 1974.
In 1994, the woman who bought the Otto home donated Robert to the Fort East Martello Museum. She claimed the doll was haunted... and had locked her in a room.
Today he sits in a glass box, holding a toy lion.
Visitors are told one rule: ask his permission before you take his picture.
Every year the museum gets letters from people apologizing to him. Asking him to lift a curse.
He's still there. Fort East Martello Museum, Key West. Would you ask permission?

borden.title: You can sleep in the murder room

slides.text: YOU CAN SLEEP IN THE ROOM WHERE IT HAPPENED
August 4, 1892. Fall River, Massachusetts. Andrew and Abby Borden were killed with a hatchet inside their own home.
The prime suspect: Andrew's daughter. Lizzie Borden. 32 years old.
Her trial gripped the whole country. The jury acquitted her.
No one else was ever convicted. People still argue about it today.
The house still stands. 230 Second Street.
Since 1996 it's been a museum... and a bed & breakfast.
The most requested room is the one where Abby was killed as she made the bed.
Thousands tour it every year. Only a few hundred are brave enough to stay the night. Would you?
